(a) CD4(+) T cells, Th2 and iNKT subsets, are critical in the pathogenesis and treatment of asthma; (b) Th2 and iNK T cells have distinct and complementary roles in asthma; and (c) Th2 and NKT cells interact to induce asthma.

CD4(+) T cells and CD1d-restricting, invariant T cell-receptor-positive, natural killer cells are both important in the development of asthma, but they are activated by different stimuli and are regulated by distinct mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the roles of Th2 cells and NKT cell in asthma pathogenesis.
understanding the roles of Th2 and iNKT cell subsets in the pathogenesis and treatment of asthma.
understanding the roles of CD4+ iNKT cells and Th2 cells in the pathophysiology of asthma and the molecular basis for their differential responsiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD4(+) NKT cells are important for asthma pathogenesis, and that their role is different from that of Th2 cells.
asthma is a heterogeneous disease that involves multiple inflammatory phenotypes and that Th2 cells, iNKT cells, and other immune cells contribute to the pathogenesis of different forms of asthma.
Th2 cells are the major effector cells of allergic asthma and are required for airway hyperresponsiveness, whereas iNKT cells are the primary cells required for the development of AHR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand the roles of T cells and NKT (iNKT cells) in asthma.
CD4(+) NKT cells are required for the development of asthma, but that they are not required for the development or maintenance of airway eosinophilic inflammation.
CD4(+) NKT cells play a central role in the pathogenesis and maintenance of AHR in both allergic and nonallergic asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD1d pathway is important for asthma and that iNKT cells are critical for AHR, the cardinal feature of asthma.
CD4(+) NKT cells are a key component of the immune system in asthma.
asthma can be induced by different immune pathways and that different forms of airway inflammation may be mediated by different cell types.
